title: Chinese Beef and Potato Stew
subtitle: 土豆炖牛肉
creator: 小麗 (教做菜)
ingredients: 500 g beef rib fingers or stewing beef
300 g potatoes, cut into rolling-cut chunks
4 slices ginger, plus 1 smashed piece for blanching
steps: Place the beef in water with one smashed piece of ginger. Bring to a boil over high heat and skim away the foam.
Heat a little oil over low heat. Melt the rock sugar until it becomes deep reddish brown.
Add the drained beef and stir-fry quickly over medium-high heat until coated and browned.
Reduce to medium-low. Add scallion, ginger, star anise, cassia and bay leaves, followed by the cooking wine, light soy sauce and dark soy sauce.
Add the tomatoes and stir-fry over medium-high heat until softened.
Add the dried hawthorn and 1 L boiling water. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce to low and stew for 1 hour 15 minutes. The reel also gives a pressure-cooker option of 15 minutes on low after pressure is reached.
Add the potatoes and continue cooking until tender. The reel marks this later stage as 15 minutes.
Add half a spoonful of salt, cover and finish over medium-low heat. Serve with rice.
evidence: Ingredient quantities and most heat settings were displayed directly in Chinese captions.
The reel gives both ordinary-pot and pressure-cooker timings.
The spoon size for salt is not specified.
The precise boundary between the beef and potato cooking stages is reconstructed from sampled frames.

title: Red Bean Wellness Porridge
subtitle: A five-ingredient Chinese sweet porridge
creator: Jia | Chinese Wellness
ingredients: Red dates or jujubes, quantity not shown
Raw red-skin peanuts, quantity not shown
Rock sugar or another crystalline sweetener, to taste
steps: Combine the red beans, red dates, peanuts, black rice and goji berries. Rinse them thoroughly.
Transfer to a lidded pot and cover generously with water.
Cook on the stovetop until the beans and grains are tender and the mixture becomes thick and dark red-purple.
Sweeten to taste. Serve warm with optional sweet fermented rice and osmanthus flowers.
evidence: The reel directly shows all five main ingredients, but only the red beans have a visible quantity.
No cooking time, water ratio or burner setting is supplied.
The sweetener appears to be rock sugar, but its label is not legible enough to confirm.
The creator presents this as pre-period wellness food. That is context, not a medical claim made by Food Vault.

title: Cucumber Sandwiches
subtitle: Herbed cream cheese tea sandwiches
creator: Cooking Classy · Jaclyn
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
8 to 10 slices fresh white, wheat or multigrain sandwich bread
steps: Whip the cream cheese with an electric hand mixer on medium-high until fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Fold in the mayonnaise, chives, parsley, dill, lemon zest, lemon juice and garlic. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread the cream cheese mixture over one side of every bread slice.
Cover half of the slices generously with cucumber. Top with the remaining bread, spread-side down.
Press lightly, trim the crusts if desired, and cut into halves or quarters. Serve immediately.
evidence: This recipe is transcribed from the source site's structured recipe card rather than inferred from video.
The source recommends a heartier sandwich bread so the generous filling holds together and cuts cleanly.
English or Persian cucumbers help limit sogginess.

title: Minced Meat with Potatoes
subtitle: 肉沫土豆
creator: Yomii Lim
ingredients: Potatoes, cut into small cubes, quantity not shown
Minced pork or chicken, quantity not shown
steps: Season the minced pork or chicken with salt and pepper.
Fry the cubed potatoes in oil until lightly golden. Remove and set aside.
Leave a little oil in the pan. Add the minced meat and stir-fry until fragrant.
Add the garlic, scallion white and chili. Stir-fry briefly.
Add water, return the fried potatoes, and season with light and dark soy sauce.
Cover and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in cornstarch slurry until the sauce thickens. Serve over rice.
evidence: The reel names every ingredient but supplies no quantities.
The only exact cooking time shown is the covered 5-minute simmer.
Either minced pork or minced chicken is explicitly offered.
The amount and ratio of light and dark soy sauce must be adjusted to taste.

title: Mushroom Goji Steamed Chicken
subtitle: Chicken steamed with shiitake, jujube and vermicelli
creator: Little kitchen🌿
ingredients: Chicken, amount and cut not specified
Dried shiitake mushrooms, amount not shown
Jujubes or red dates, amount not shown
Hot water and salt, for brining
steps: Soak the shiitake mushrooms and goji berries in water for 15 minutes. Reserve the mushroom soaking water.
Brine the chicken in hot salted water, then place it in a heatproof shallow bowl.
Arrange the soaked shiitake, jujubes and goji berries around the chicken.
Add a little reserved mushroom soaking water. Season with salt and chicken bouillon.
Place the bowl in a covered steamer and steam for 30 to 40 minutes.
Add the vermicelli and steam for another 5 minutes, until tender.
evidence: The reel directly shows the 15-minute soak and 30-to-40-minute steaming time.
The creator's written caption supplies the hot-water brine, seasonings and final 5-minute vermicelli step.
No ingredient quantities are supplied.
The reel frames this as comfort food when feeling under the weather, not as medical treatment.

title: Rice Cooker Black Glutinous Rice Tapioca
subtitle: A coconut milk dessert made without the stovetop
creator: Drew Eats 🍛
ingredients: Black glutinous rice, quantity not shown
Small tapioca pearls, quantity not shown
steps: Rinse the black glutinous rice and soak it overnight.
Drain and cook the rice in a rice cooker using its quickest setting, until tender.
Add the tapioca pearls, rock sugar, coconut milk and water. Stir well.
Run the quickest rice-cooker setting again for no more than 20 minutes, stopping early if needed so the tapioca remains intact.
Stir and serve warm. If the pudding is too thick, loosen it with boiling water or additional coconut milk.
evidence: The reel directly shows the overnight soak, one initial rice-cooker cycle and a second 20-minute cooking stage.
The creator's caption warns not to exceed 20 minutes after adding tapioca.
No ingredient quantities or liquid ratios are supplied.
The final texture is intended to be thick, soft and spoonable.

title: Korean Braised Chicken
subtitle: Jjimdak · 찜닭
creator: Angela | SF Food & Lifestyle
ingredients: 2 medium white or Yukon Gold potatoes, about 10 oz
3 to 4 mushroom caps, rehydrated dried shiitake or fresh mushrooms
2 to 3 dried whole red chili peppers, or 4 to 5 small ones
1 to 2 fresh chili peppers or jalapeños, optional
2 tbsp oyster sauce, or additional soy sauce
2 tbsp rice wine, mirim or mirin
2 tbsp dark brown sugar, or regular sugar
3 to 4 tbsp corn syrup, rice syrup or oligo syrup, or 2 to 3 tbsp honey
steps: Soak the sweet potato starch noodles in warm water for about 30 minutes, then drain well.
Trim excess fat from the chicken. Cut the potatoes into 1 1/2-inch chunks and soak them in water. Cut the carrot, mushrooms and onion into bite-size pieces.

Place the chicken in a large pot and add 3 cups water. Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce, rice wine, sugar, syrup or honey, and black pepper. Bring to a boil uncovered over high heat. Boil for about 10 minutes and skim off the foam.
Add the potatoes, carrot, mushrooms, onion, dried chilies, garlic and ginger. Cover and cook for 8 to 10 minutes.
Gently mix in the fresh chilies, scallions and drained noodles. Cook uncovered for about 3 minutes, until the noodles are tender and glossy.
Stir in the sesame oil, sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve hot.
evidence: The reel caption directly supplies the complete ingredient list and quantities except for the 3 cups of cooking water.
The video directly shows chicken, water, braising sauce, vegetables, mushrooms and noodles being added in that order.
The reel does not display cooking times. The timing and 3 cups of water come from Korean Bapsang's recipe, whose ingredient list matches the caption exactly.
The creator describes this as an easy one-pot recipe.
